title: spike: can the AI place my dictated words into the five fields without inventing any?
description:
## Goal

Find out, before building any of voice-brief, whether a Claude model can take my dictated words
about an idea and place them into the five fields of a task prompt (Weakest part, Force,
Smallest move, Preserves, Would reverse it), keeping what I said apart from what it adds, and asking instead of
inventing when my words leave a field empty. The whole app (sort, revise, review, grade, ask; see
`design.md`) rests on this. If the model cannot do it reliably, the UI is not worth building yet.

This is a spike: throwaway code, a measured verdict. It is not the app.

## Diagnosis (cm-dr0)

Nothing exists yet. The weakest part is the riskiest assumption, not the plumbing: capture,
Herdr, celld and the TUI are solved problems; faithful placement with said/added tags and no
invented fields is not. Smallest move: measure it on a few real dictations before writing any UI.

## Hypothesis and its refutation (cm-gi3, stated before anything runs)

**Hypothesis.** Given only the transcript of me talking through an idea, the model returns the five
fields such that (a) every claim I made appears, in a field, tagged `said` with a transcript span
that supports it; (b) everything it adds is tagged `added`; (c) a field my words do not fill comes
back empty with a question to me, not filled.

**Refuted if any of these happens** in the recorded runs:

1. A claim on the operator-confirmed claim list is missing from the output.
2. A claim tagged `said` is not supported by its cited span, or the span is not in the transcript.
3. A field the confirmed annotation marks as empty comes back filled, whether tagged `said` or
   `added`.

Measured and reported, not refuting (the operator judges them, cm-gkl): claims placed in a
different field than the annotation; my own words tagged `added` (over-flagging); variance across
runs.

## The format (from `idea.md`)

| Field | What it says |
|---|---|
| Weakest part | Where the current whole is weakest: a specific component, file or step |
| Force | The pressure that is unresolved there |
| Smallest move | The one change that resolves the force and leaves the rest intact |
| Preserves | What the change must leave intact |
| Would reverse it | The observable result that would show the change was wrong |

Weakest part, force and smallest move come from cm-dr0; preserves and would reverse it from
cm-e2y.

## Facts already established (2026-10-25)

- There are no golden cases: `examples.md` held `CLAUDE.md` rule sections, an output the app no
  longer makes, and was deleted (still in git at `00fb800`). The corpus is new dictations.
- Claude Code loads `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` into every session, `claude -p` included. The production
  job will run on celld with an explicit prompt and no `CLAUDE.md`, so a spike that runs with my
  `CLAUDE.md` loaded measures a different system.
- Candidate ideas already discussed in my own words this session: splitting out `vbd`; git as the
  record; celld and pi-durable for long-running jobs; deleting `examples.md`.

## Scope

In: one task (transcript → five fields with tags and questions), a validator, a checker, red-first
tests of both, recorded runs, a findings document.

Out (separate beads later): revise and review flows, grading, voxtype and `pw-record`, Herdr,
celld and pi-durable, the TUI. The prompt and output contract should be written so they can move
into the celld `IdeaCell` job later, but nothing in the spike runs on celld.

## Operator decision

My words, 2026-10-25:

- "ready to file beads, follow /beads-workflow for this spike"
- "this is a dictation app, to develop my idea using my microphone and AI in the format that I
  want: Weakest part, Force, Preserves, Would reverse it, format."
- "building a task prompt for the agent is the idea."
- "Weakest part, force, smallest move come from cm-dr0 … Preserves, would reverse it come from
  cm-e2y … Smallest move stays."
- From `idea.md`: AI work runs on Claude, not the local model; nothing is written without my
  accept.

What this approves: filing this epic and its children, and building throwaway spike code in this
repo under `spike/`.

Nothing else is approved. None: every other policy question goes back to the operator. In
particular these are **not** decided and must be asked, not assumed: the model id used for the verdict (assumption, flagged: `claude-opus-5-5`,
recorded with each run); the number of runs per transcript; whether an LLM judge may stand in for
operator judgement; the spike's language (TypeScript suggested, so the contract moves to celld
unchanged). Children inherit this section.

## Children and order

1. Corpus: my dictations and an operator-confirmed annotation.
2. Model calls see only the explicit prompt, as the celld job will.
3. Output contract and deterministic validator.
4. Checker against the annotation.
5. See validator and checker fail on planted defects.
6. Run and record the verdict in `docs/findings.md`.

1 and 2 block 3; 3 blocks 4; 4 blocks 5; 5 blocks 6.

## Done means

`docs/findings.md` states, per refutation criterion, whether it fired, with run ids and verbatim
excerpts as evidence, and the operator has read it. "Refuted" is a valid outcome (cm-xzq).

title: spike: corpus of my dictations with an operator-confirmed annotation
description:
## What

A small corpus of my own dictations about real ideas, each with an annotation I have confirmed.
Every later bead scores against it; if the annotation is wrong, every verdict is wrong (cm-la6).

## Contents

- **Transcripts:** at least four, of me talking through an idea as I would into the app: rambling,
  out of order, typos and fillers kept. At least one must leave Would reverse it unsaid and one
  must leave Preserves unsaid, so refutation 3 has something to catch. Candidates from this
  session: splitting out `vbd`; git as the record; celld for long-running jobs; deleting
  `examples.md`. The transcripts can be typed or dictated; voxtype is not set up for the app yet,
  and the spike does not depend on it.
- **Annotation per transcript:**
  - the claims I made, each with its verbatim transcript span;
  - the field each claim belongs to (one of the five, or none: context that is not part of the
    prompt);
  - which fields my words leave empty.
- **Confirmation record:** the date and my words confirming the annotation, or my corrections.

## Who does what

I provide the transcripts. The agent may draft the annotation; it counts only after I confirm it,
so the spike does not grade itself. An Artifact for confirming it (transcript with spans
highlighted, each claim with its field and a toggle) is a good fit (cm-cdv), with my answers stored
where the agent can read them back.

## Acceptance

- Every annotated span is a verbatim substring of its transcript (checked by code; see that check
  fail first on a span that is not in the transcript, cm-yzv).
- The corpus has at least one transcript with Would reverse it empty and one with Preserves empty.
- The operator has confirmed the annotation; until then this bead stays in_progress (cm-nvh).
- Files under `spike/corpus/`, one move per commit (cm-uom), scoped messages (cm-qqz).

## Operator decision

Inherited from the epic. Providing transcripts and confirming the annotation are operator actions.

title: spike: model calls see only the explicit prompt, as the celld job will
description:
## What

Every model call the spike makes sees only an explicit prompt: the instructions, the field
definitions and the transcript. Not `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, project instructions, auto-memory, the
working directory, or the corpus annotation.

## Why

The production job runs on celld with an explicit prompt and nothing else. Claude Code loads
`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` into every session, `claude -p` included, and that file is full of rules
about forces, weakest parts and falsifiable conditions that would help the model. A spike that runs
with it loaded measures a different, better-briefed system, and its verdict would not transfer
(cm-la6). The annotation must stay out of context for the obvious reason.

## Acceptance

- **Red first (cm-yzv):** with the default setup, a canary prompt ("quote rule cm-la6") shows the
  model can see `CLAUDE.md`. Record that run.
- With isolation on, the same canary shows it cannot. Record that run.
- The mechanism is written down, with how a reader can confirm nothing else was loaded.

## Operator decision

Inherited from the epic. The mechanism is an implementation choice; spending money on API calls
instead of the subscription is not, so ask before switching to paid API usage.

title: spike: five-field output contract and deterministic validator
description:
## What

The output contract for the one task the spike measures, the prompt for it, and a deterministic
validator. All model calls go through the isolation from `.2`.

**Input:** a transcript. **Output:** the five fields (Weakest part, Force, Smallest move,
Preserves, Would reverse it). Each field is either:

- a list of claims, each with an id stable within the output and a tag:
  - `said`, with one or more transcript spans that support it; or
  - `added`, with a one-line reason (inference, generalisation, new claim); or
- empty, with a question to me that would let me fill it.

## Why

The said/added tag is the product (`design.md`: every proposal shows whether it came from my
words), and "ask, don't invent" is the rule for empty fields. A structured contract lets code check
what code can (cm-8gv) and leaves only judgement to people.

## Validator (deterministic)

Rejects an output when:

- it does not match the schema, or a field is missing;
- a `said` span is not a verbatim substring of the transcript (state the whitespace and quote
  normalisation, if any, and test it);
- a field is empty and has no question, or has both claims and a question.

## Acceptance

- Validator tests cover zero, one and many claims and spans per field (cm-srn); each rejection rule
  has a test that sees it fire (cm-yzv); each test has cyclomatic complexity 1 (cm-o9o).
- Mutation testing on the validator kills the mutants, or each survivor is classified as
  equivalent with a reason (cm-1qk, cm-j6g).
- The prompt and schema live in files of their own under `spike/`, written to move into the celld
  `IdeaCell` job later without rewriting.
- The model id and parameters are configuration, recorded with every call (open question in the
  epic).

## Operator decision

Inherited from the epic.

title: spike: checker scoring outputs against the annotation
description:
## What

A checker that scores each output against the confirmed annotation and reports the epic's
refutation criteria per transcript and run.

- **Coverage (judged):** each confirmed claim appears in some field.
- **Support (judged):** each `said` claim is supported by its span (that the span exists is the
  validator's job).
- **Empty fields (code):** each field the annotation marks empty comes back empty with a question.
- **Placement (judged, reported):** claims in a different field than the annotation.
- **Over-flagging (judged, reported):** confirmed claims of mine tagged `added`.

## Judgement

The judged items need my judgement or a stand-in I have approved. Provide an instrument (cm-cdv,
cm-wue): an Artifact over the real run data showing the transcript with cited spans highlighted,
the output fields, and the judged questions, with my answers stored where the checker reads them
back. An LLM judge may be proposed, but only with its agreement with my judgements on a known
subset reported (cm-27o), and only used if I approve it.

## Acceptance

- Output per transcript and run: each refutation criterion fired or not, the claim ids involved,
  verbatim excerpts; placement and over-flagging counts.
- Code-scored parts have tests over zero, one and many claims and fields (cm-srn), and mutation
  testing (cm-1qk).
- The instrument is run on a case with a known answer before anyone trusts it (cm-27o); that is
  `.5`, which this bead blocks.

## Operator decision

Inherited from the epic. Whether an LLM judge may replace any operator judgement is an operator
decision.

title: spike: see validator and checker fail on planted defects
description:
## What

Before any real run counts, show that the validator, the checker and the judging instrument each
fail on planted defects and pass on a known-good input.

## Why

A gate that has never failed is unproven (cm-yzv); an instrument can lie (cm-27o). "The model
passes" is exactly the result that most needs a proven checker (cm-la6).

## Planted cases (minimum)

1. The confirmed annotation rendered as if it were model output: scores perfectly (known-good).
2. One confirmed claim removed: refutation 1 fires and names it.
3. A `said` span not in the transcript: the validator rejects it.
4. A `said` claim whose span exists but does not support it: refutation 2 fires (judged; the
   instrument shows it and records the judgement).
5. A field the annotation marks empty, filled with an `added` claim: refutation 3 fires.
6. The same field filled with a `said` claim: refutation 3 fires.
7. A claim moved to another field: placement reports it.
8. An empty field without a question: the validator rejects it.

## Acceptance

- Each planted case was run and its output recorded under `spike/results/red/`, showing the
  expected fail (or pass for case 1).
- Any case that did not fail as expected is a checker defect, fixed and re-run before this bead
  closes, with a test added for it (cm-104).

## Operator decision

Inherited from the epic.

title: spike: run the corpus and record the verdict in docs/findings.md
description:
## What

Run the task on every corpus transcript, several times each, through the isolation, validator and
checker; record everything; write the verdict in `docs/findings.md`.

## Before running (ask, don't assume)

The epic leaves these to the operator: the model id (assumption flagged: `claude-opus-5-5`), the
number of runs per transcript, and whether any LLM judge may stand in for operator judgement. Get
the answers and record them, with the date, in the findings.

## Record per run

Model id and parameters, prompt and schema version (commit), the full input as sent, the raw
output, validator and checker results, latency and token usage. Raw outputs are committed under
`spike/results/<run-id>/` so every number in the findings can be traced to a file.

## `docs/findings.md`

In the style of `~/Projects/mine/voice-command-bar/docs/02-findings.md`: what was measured, on
what, which claims did not survive.

- The hypothesis and the three refutation criteria, quoted from the epic.
- Per criterion: fired or not, in which transcripts and runs, with verbatim excerpts.
- Placement disagreements and over-flagging, and how they vary across runs.
- Latency and tokens per call, to size the celld job later.
- What it means for `design.md`: if the hypothesis survives, which prompt and contract move into
  the `IdeaCell` job; if refuted, what failed and what could be tried next (a different contract,
  a two-pass place-then-audit, a different model).
- Explicit limits: a handful of transcripts is a small corpus; these are runs, not a benchmark.

## Acceptance

- Every number in the findings links to a run directory.
- No run is excluded without the exclusion and its reason written in the findings.
- The verdict is stated either way; "refuted" closes this bead as well as "survived" does
  (cm-xzq). The operator has read the findings; what to build next is the operator's call (cm-gkl).

## Operator decision

Inherited from the epic.
